name: timesheet-payroll
requirements: T1 Package `clock` provides `type Minutes int`, `func ParseDuration(s string) (Minutes, error)` and `func (m Minutes) String() string`. Staff record time worked as hours and minutes. `ParseDuration` accepts one or two ASCII hour digits, a colon, and exactly two ASCII minute digits from `00` to `59`, and nothing else. Examples: `7:30`, `07:30`, `0:05`, `00:00` and `99:59` are accepted. It returns the total in minutes, so `7:30` gives 450 and `99:59` gives 5999. Every other input returns 0 and an error for which `errors.Is(err, clock.ErrInvalidDuration)` is true. This includes the empty string, any whitespace, a sign, three hour digits, a single minute digit, minutes of `60` or more, and a missing colon. `String` formats the value as the hour count with no padding, a colon, and two-digit minutes: 0 gives `0:00`, 5 gives `0:05`, 450 gives `7:30` and 6000 gives `100:00`. A negative value is formatted from its absolute value and prefixed with `-`, so -90 gives `-1:30`.

T2 Package `clock` provides `func ParseDate(s string) (time.Time, error)` and `func WeekStart(t time.Time) time.Time`. `ParseDate` accepts exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`, with a year from 0001 to 9999 and two-digit month and day, naming a real calendar date. It returns midnight UTC on that date, in location `time.UTC`. `2028-02-29` is accepted. `2026-02-29`, `2026-13-01`, `0000-01-01`, `2026-1-05`, `2026/01/05`, any leading or trailing whitespace, and the empty string are rejected. A rejected input returns a zero `time.Time` and an error for which `errors.Is(err, clock.ErrInvalidDate)` is true. `WeekStart` takes the calendar date of t in UTC. It returns midnight UTC, in location `time.UTC`, on the Monday of the Monday-to-Sunday week containing that date. Examples: `2026-11-08` (a Sunday) gives `2026-11-02`. `2026-11-09` (a Monday) gives `2026-11-09`. `2026-11-09T23:59:00Z` gives `2026-11-09`. `2027-01-01` (a Friday) gives `2026-12-28`.

T3 Package `money` provides `type Cents int64`, `func ParseAmount(s string) (Cents, error)` and `func (c Cents) String() string`. Pay rates are entered in dollars and cents. `ParseAmount` accepts 1 to 9 ASCII digits, optionally followed by `.` and exactly two ASCII digits, and nothing else. Examples: `25` gives 2500, `25.50` gives 2550, `0.99` gives 99 and `007.00` gives 700. Rejected inputs return 0 and an error for which `errors.Is(err, money.ErrInvalidAmount)` is true. These include the empty string, `.50`, `25.`, `25.5`, `25.505`, `-1.00`, `+1.00`, `1,000.00`, `1e3`, ten integer digits, and any whitespace. `String` formats the value with the whole-dollar part grouped in threes by commas, then `.`, then exactly two cent digits. Examples: 0 gives `0.00`, 5 gives `0.05`, 2550 gives `25.50`, 105625 gives `1,056.25` and 123456789 gives `1,234,567.89`. A negative value is prefixed with `-`: -1200 gives `-12.00` and -123456 gives `-1,234.56`. The minimum int64 value must not panic and gives `-92,233,720,368,547,758.08`.

T4 Package `entry` provides `type Entry struct { Date time.Time; Employee string; Worked clock.Minutes }`, `func ValidEmployee(id string) bool` and `func ParseEntry(line string) (Entry, error)`. An employee ID is valid when all of the following hold: it is 1 to 32 bytes long, it starts with a lowercase ASCII letter, and it contains only lowercase ASCII letters, ASCII digits and `-`. `ValidEmployee` reports whether an ID is valid. `alice` and `j-smith2` are valid. The empty string, `Alice`, `2pac`, `j_smith`, `-bob` and a 33-letter ID are invalid. A timesheet line has exactly three comma-separated fields: date, employee ID and time worked, for example `2026-11-02,alice,7:30`. Spaces and tabs around each field are ignored, so `2026-11-02 , alice , 7:30` is valid. The date must be `YYYY-MM-DD` naming a real calendar date. The employee ID must be valid. The time must be one or two hour digits, a colon and two minute digits from 00 to 59, and it must be greater than `0:00` and at most `24:00`. On success, Date is midnight UTC on the given date. Fields are checked in the order date, employee, time, and the error describes the first failing field. Every failure returns a zero Entry and an error for which `errors.Is(err, entry.ErrInvalidEntry)` is true. When the date field is malformed, `errors.Is(err, clock.ErrInvalidDate)` is also true. When the time field is malformed, `errors.Is(err, clock.ErrInvalidDuration)` is also true. `0:00` and `24:01` are well-formed times that are out of range, so only `ErrInvalidEntry` applies to them. A line with fewer or more than three fields, including one with a trailing comma, is invalid.

T5 Package `entry` provides `func ParseEntries(r io.Reader) ([]Entry, error)`, which reads a whole timesheet file. Lines are separated by `\n`, a trailing `\r` on a line is ignored, and a final line without a newline is still read. Some lines are skipped: a line that is empty or contains only spaces and tabs, and a line whose first character other than a space or tab is `#`. Every other line must be a valid timesheet line, with the format and rules given in T4. At the first invalid line, `ParseEntries` returns nil and an error whose message begins with `line N: `. N is the 1-based line number in the file, counting skipped lines. The error wraps the line's error, so the `errors.Is` checks from T4 still hold. The same employee may not appear twice on the same date. The second occurrence fails with nil entries and an error whose message is exactly `line N: duplicate entry for <employee> on <YYYY-MM-DD>`, for example `line 4: duplicate entry for alice on 2026-11-02`. For this error, `errors.Is(err, entry.ErrDuplicateEntry)` is true and `errors.Is(err, entry.ErrInvalidEntry)` is false. On success, entries are returned in file order. A file with no entry lines returns an empty, non-nil slice and a nil error. If reading from r fails, `ParseEntries` returns nil and an error that wraps the read error.

T6 Package `payroll` provides `type WeekSummary struct { Employee string; WeekStart time.Time; Regular clock.Minutes; Overtime clock.Minutes }` and `func Summarize(entries []entry.Entry) []WeekSummary`. Summarize groups entries by employee and by Monday-to-Sunday week. A week is identified by midnight UTC, in location `time.UTC`, on its Monday, taken from the entry's date in UTC. In each group, the first 40:00 (2400 minutes) of total Worked time is Regular and anything above it is Overtime. A total of 41:30 gives Regular 40:00 and Overtime 1:30. A total of exactly 40:00 gives Overtime 0:00. A total of 12:15 gives Regular 12:15 and Overtime 0:00. Overtime depends only on the weekly total, so a long single day is not overtime by itself. An entry on Sunday 2026-11-08 and one on Monday 2026-11-09 fall in different weeks, with WeekStart 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-09. Summarize returns one WeekSummary for each (employee, week) pair that has at least one entry. Results are sorted by Employee in ascending byte order, then by WeekStart ascending. The order of the input does not affect the result, and the input slice is not modified. Empty or nil input returns an empty, non-nil slice. Worked values are summed as given, without validation.

T7 Package `payroll` provides `func WeekPay(rate money.Cents, s WeekSummary) money.Cents`. Here rate is an hourly rate in cents. Regular time is paid at rate per hour, and overtime is paid at one and a half times rate per hour. The pay is computed exactly and rounded once at the end, to the nearest cent, with exact halves rounded up. This is equivalent to rate × (2 × Regular + 3 × Overtime) / 120, with Regular and Overtime in minutes, rounded half up. Examples:
- rate 2500, Regular 40:00, Overtime 1:30 gives 105625.
- rate 2500, Regular 12:15 gives 30625.
- rate 1999, Regular 0:07 gives 233 (exact value 233.216…).
- rate 1, Regular 0:30 gives 1 (exact value 0.5).
- rate 1, Overtime 0:10 gives 0 (exact value 0.25).
- rate 3, Overtime 0:10 gives 1 (exact value 0.75).
- rate 0 gives 0.
If rate, Regular or Overtime is negative, the result is 0. The result must be exact for every rate up to 99,999,999,999 and every Regular + Overtime up to 10,080 minutes.

T8 Package `payroll` provides `func ParseRates(r io.Reader) (map[string]money.Cents, error)`, which reads the hourly rate file. Lines are separated by `\n`, a trailing `\r` is ignored, and a final line without a newline is still read. Some lines are skipped: a line that is empty or contains only spaces and tabs, and a line whose first character other than a space or tab is `#`. Every other line has the form `<employee>=<amount>` and is split at its first `=`. Spaces and tabs around the employee ID and around the amount are ignored, so `alice = 25.00` is valid. The employee ID must be valid: 1 to 32 bytes, starting with a lowercase ASCII letter, and containing only lowercase ASCII letters, ASCII digits and `-`. The amount must be 1 to 9 ASCII digits, optionally followed by `.` and exactly two digits, and it must be greater than 0. Each employee may appear only once. At the first bad line, `ParseRates` returns nil and an error whose message begins with `line N: `. N is the 1-based line number, counting skipped lines. For this error, `errors.Is(err, payroll.ErrInvalidRate)` is true. When the amount is malformed, for example `alice=2=5` or `alice=25.5`, `errors.Is(err, money.ErrInvalidAmount)` is also true. `0.00` is well-formed, so only `ErrInvalidRate` applies to it. Bad lines include a missing `=`, an empty ID, an invalid ID, a malformed amount, a zero amount and a repeated employee. On success, `ParseRates` returns a map with one key for each rate line. A file with no rate lines returns an empty, non-nil map and a nil error. If reading from r fails, `ParseRates` returns nil and an error that wraps the read error.

T9 Package `report` provides `func Weekly(entries io.Reader, rates io.Reader) (string, error)`. It produces the weekly payroll report from a timesheet file in the format of T5 and a rate file in the format of T8.

Errors. The timesheet is read and checked before the rate file. If the timesheet is invalid, `Weekly` returns an empty string and an error whose message is `entries: ` followed by the timesheet error's message, and the error wraps the timesheet error. An invalid rate file is reported the same way with the prefix `rates: `. Some employees may have timesheet entries but no rate. In that case `Weekly` returns an empty string and an error whose message is exactly `missing rate for <id>`, naming the first such employee in byte order. For this error, `errors.Is(err, report.ErrMissingRate)` is true. Rates for employees without entries are ignored.

Layout. The report starts with a header line. It then has one row for each (employee, week) pair that has entries, sorted by employee in ascending byte order and then by week ascending. It ends with a TOTAL line. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`, and no line has trailing spaces. The columns, in order and separated by exactly two spaces, are:
- WEEK: the Monday's date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, left-aligned, width 10.
- EMPLOYEE: left-aligned, width W, where W is the larger of 8 and the length of the longest employee ID in the report.
- REGULAR: right-aligned, width 7.
- OVERTIME: right-aligned, width 8.
- PAY: right-aligned, width 12.
REGULAR and OVERTIME are the week's regular and overtime time, with the first 40:00 of each employee's week regular and the rest overtime. They are formatted as unpadded hours, a colon and two-digit minutes, for example `0:00`, `1:30` or `100:00`. PAY is the week's pay at the employee's rate. Regular time is paid at the rate per hour and overtime at 1.5 times the rate per hour, rounded once to the nearest cent with halves rounded up. It is formatted with comma-grouped dollars and two decimals, for example `1,056.25`. A value longer than its column width is printed in full and pushes the rest of the line to the right.

Header and TOTAL lines. The header line contains `WEEK`, `EMPLOYEE`, `REGULAR`, `OVERTIME` and `PAY`, with the same widths and alignment as the columns. The TOTAL line has `TOTAL` in the WEEK column and spaces to width W in the EMPLOYEE column. Its REGULAR and OVERTIME columns hold the sums of those columns. Its PAY column holds the sum of the rows' rounded pays. A timesheet with no entries produces only the header line and a TOTAL line showing `0:00`, `0:00` and `0.00`.

Example. The timesheet has these lines:
- `2026-11-02,alice,9:00`
- `2026-11-03,alice,9:00`
- `2026-11-04,alice,9:00`
- `2026-11-05,alice,9:00`
- `2026-11-06,alice,5:30`
- `2026-11-04,bob,12:15`
The rate file has the lines `alice=25.00` and `bob=25.00`. `Weekly` returns exactly these four lines, each ending with `\n`:
WEEK        EMPLOYEE  REGULAR  OVERTIME           PAY
2026-11-02  alice       40:00      1:30      1,056.25
2026-11-02  bob         12:15      0:00        306.25
TOTAL                   52:15      1:30      1,362.50

allocation.A: Developer A owns the clock package (T1, T2), the entry package (T4, T5) and the report package (T9), and works in this order: finish and hand off T1 and T2 first because B's T6 needs `WeekStart`; then T4, so B has `Entry` and `ValidEmployee` for T6 and T8; then T5; and finally T9, once B has delivered T6 to T8.
allocation.B: Developer B owns the money package (T3) and the payroll package (T6, T7, T8), and works in this order: finish and hand off T3 first because A's T9 needs `Cents.String`; then T7, which needs only T3 and the `WeekSummary` type already in the skeleton; then T6 once A's T2 has landed; then T8 once A's T4 has landed, handing T6 to T8 to A for T9.

requirements: Correction to T2: `WeekStart` must return midnight UTC on the last Monday strictly before the date, not on the Monday on or before it. When the date is itself a Monday, the result is the Monday seven days earlier: 2026-11-09 (a Monday) gives 2026-11-02, not 2026-11-09, and so does 2026-11-09T23:59:00Z. Every other day is unchanged: 2026-11-08 (a Sunday) still gives 2026-11-02, and 2026-11-10 (a Tuesday) gives 2026-11-09.
